subject: Security notice: transient auth failures for hosted API (evidence + action plan)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@clearbank.com>; ClearBank Security <sec@clearbank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Security notice: transient auth failures for hosted API (evidence + action plan)

Hi Alex / ClearBank team —

Quick heads-up: between ~08:43 ET and 08:58 ET today we observed a spike in 401/403 errors for requests originating from your region (us-east-1) for the Redwood hosted inference API. The hit rate peaked at ~4.5% of requests for a ~15-minute window and impacted a small subset of tokens tied to your integration.

What we did immediately:
- Scoped and throttled the affected token pool (fall back to read-only routing for in-flight requests).
- Rotated the short-lived signing keys for the service that issues API tokens.
- Captured auth traces and a KV-cache snapshot for forensic review. Attached preliminary artifacts (redwood_auth_trace.csv, kv-cache-snapshot.tar.gz).

Next steps we are undertaking (ETA inlined):
- Full forensic analysis + timeline (48 hrs).
- Postmortem and evidence package for your security team (by 2026-11-17 EOD).
- Confirm whether any data exfiltration or model prompt leakage occurred (we have found no evidence so far).

Requested info from you: can you confirm whether you saw elevated client-side retries or error rates at the same times? That will help correlate client vs platform.

I’m copying our security lead (neha_kapoor) and infra lead (karthik_iyer) to coordinate.

Apologies for the disruption — we take this seriously and will share a full timeline and remediation details.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@clearbank.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: sec@clearbank.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:34:12 -0500
Subject: Re: Security notice: transient auth failures for hosted API (evidence + action plan)

Thanks Rishi — we saw customer-facing errors and spike in retries on our side starting ~08:45 ET; several retries led to duplicate requests for some flows. No PII was written to third-party storage, and our SREs rate-limited clients and patched the retry logic as a stop-gap.

We appreciate the quick mitigation. Please include any indicators of compromise (IoCs) you find. Also, we need the postmortem and the full artifact bundle for our internal audit by 2026-11-19.

Alex
Alex Jones
ClearBank — Head of Integrations
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@clearbank.com>; ClearBank Security <sec@clearbank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 11:05:23 -0500
Subject: Re: Security notice: transient auth failures for hosted API (evidence + action plan)

Alex — thanks for confirming. A couple of immediate clarifications and timeline items: 

1) Root cause (prelim): a race condition during our short-lived token refresh path combined with an upstream rate-limiter misclassification caused ~0.8% of valid refresh requests to be rejected. That triggered downstream 401s for tokens that should have been valid for another 60s.

2) Containment we applied (complete):
   - Reverted the recent routing change in the token service (rolled back at 09:12 ET).
   - Forced refresh for affected tokens and disabled the flawed rate-limiter rule.
   - Enabled request-level tracing for all calls from ClearBank for 72 hours.

3) Evidence attached: redwood_auth_trace.csv (auth logs, scrubbed IPs), kv-cache-snapshot.tar.gz (service-side KV state at the time). We also logged syscall-level traces for the token-service and put a redacted forensic summary in forensic-summary-20261117.pdf (attached to the final PM).

4) Immediate mitigation recommended for you: implement exponential backoff with jitter (if not already) and dedupe client-side when a retry returns success).

I’ll follow up with a full postmortem and the SOC2-friendly evidence bundle (signed integrity checks) by EOD on Tue 2026-11-17. If you need the artifacts earlier for audit, let me know and we’ll expedite.

—Rishi
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@clearbank.com>; ClearBank Security <sec@clearbank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:48:00 -0500
Subject: Postmortem: transient auth refresh race -> elevated 401s (final evidence package)

Alex / ClearBank security —

Attached is the final postmortem and evidence bundle (forensic-summary-20261117.pdf). Executive summary:

- Incident window: 2026-11-15T08:43:12Z -> 2026-11-15T08:58:21Z
- Impact: ~4.5% spike in 401/403 responses for requests using affected token refresh path; no unauthorized data access detected.
- Root cause: race between token refresh fast-path and a new heuristics-based rate-limiter that incorrectly classified certain refresh calls as abusive.
- Actions completed: rollback of routing change, key rotation for short-lived signing keys, disabled offending rate-limiter rule, post-deployment canary for token paths, and a new unit+integration test to cover the race.

Attached artifacts include: redwood_auth_trace.csv, kv-cache-snapshot.tar.gz, forensic-summary-20261117.pdf, signed checksums, and a link to the Jira ticket (SEC-4921).

Compliance note: we have compiled the artifacts in SOC 2-friendly format and validated chain-of-custody for the evidence. If your compliance team needs additional attestations (e.g., notarized timestamp, HSM audit log excerpts) please tell us and we will arrange.

Open items:
- Marissa: please confirm whether we want to schedule a cross-team review with ClearBank security next week (30 min).
- Neha: please run final integrity checks and share any additional redaction for the artifact bundle.
- Karthik: confirm that the token-service test coverage and canary are in the next deploy window (target: 2026-11-22).

Thanks for the close coordination.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
